extracted.intended_audience: visual artists/illustrators seeking to submit artwork to Strange Horizons magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for artists who want their work commissioned or selected to accompany fiction in Strange Horizons; covers what the editors look for, what they reject, submission format, pay, and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art must tell a story
rubrics_metrics.description: We commission art that tells a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artwork will be commissioned or selected by the fiction editors to accompany the story's tone and content. To tell that story, use all the tools at your command: color, composition, lighting, and detail. Browse previous issues and art archives to see examples of what they buy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full color, depth, texture, and thoughtful composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Full color work with depth, texture, and thoughtful composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Yes, please' as a preferred quality; demonstrates technical richness and careful arrangement of visual elements appropriate for editorial illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work that evokes an emotion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred quality: art should make the viewer feel something relevant to the story rather than being purely decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work that captures a moment in time
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that captures a moment in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred quality: imagery that implies narrative context or a decisive instant helps align the piece with the fiction it accompanies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and mood
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred quality: illustrations should convey character presence and an overall mood that complements the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual approaches to figure, line, and color
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual approaches to figure, line, and color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred quality: original or unexpected stylistic choices that show distinct artistic voice and suit speculative fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred quality: inventive concepts and visual thinking that enrich the speculative aspects of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard sells (styles they generally will not buy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cartoons/anime; line art/black and white; portraits/fan commissions; photography; collage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Hard sells' — these formats or styles are generally not acceptable for commission as accompanying artwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid gratuitous sexualization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'No, thank you' as disallowed content; editors will not accept works that sexualize subjects gratuitously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common SF tropes (uninspired stock imagery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common SF tropes like shiny distant cities with huge planets behind them — not desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'No, thank you' as clichéd subject matter to avoid; editors seek fresh imagery rather than overused speculative visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping, fetishization, and objectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Stereotyping, fetishization, or objectification of people are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'No, thank you' — submissions that rely on harmful or reductive portrayals of people will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Send a link to ONE portfolio (if available) and THREE examples of your work; example images as links or attached .png or .jpg, not more than 1000x1000 pixels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email submissions to art@strangehorizons.com. Use 'ARTIST SUBMISSION: Artist Name' in the subject line. The three samples should be the best fit for the magazine and show you understand these guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response policy and update frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: They will retain artist information but will only contact you if they wish to commission or use an existing piece; they buy only 12 pieces per year so many artists may never hear back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lack of response is not a judgment on quality. Artists are welcome to send updates, but only every 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment for art: $200 for an original work commissioned to accompany a story, $100 if they use a piece from an artist's existing portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear compensation levels depending on whether the work is commissioned or taken from a portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights purchased and artist retention of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: They buy the right to display the selected artwork with the story and to archive it on their website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For commissioned original work, artists retain all rights to use the work for merchandise or to post the work elsewhere once the story is live, but are asked to wait until the story is live before re-selling the work and to credit it as originally appearing for the story. They may optionally ask for rights to use the work for limited-run, not-for-sale promotional printed items (e.g., flyers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection tied to story tone and content (monthly commissioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange Horizons publishes original art alongside one story each month; artwork is commissioned or selected by fiction editors to accompany the story's tone and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is editorial and narrative-driven — matching the specific story is a central criterion rather than generic marketability.
